contracts.commit_point: return handler(request) at app.py:106 — the middleware's forwarding call; once reached, the tool body executes and its external HTTP requests are issued (app.py:33 for get_weather; app.py:57-61 for get_news).
contracts.declared_mechanism: The @wrap_tool_call-decorated middleware human_approval (app.py:93-94) intercepts tool calls; it records request.tool_call['name'] in st.session_state['last_tool'] (app.py:95-98), returns a denial ToolMessage when st.session_state.get('approve', True) is falsy (app.py:100-104), and otherwise forwards via return handler(request) (app.py:106). It is registered on the agent via create_agent(llm, tools=[get_weather, get_news], middleware=[human_approval]) (app.py:112-117), and the flag it reads is set by the sidebar checkbox bound to key 'approve' (app.py:129-131).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An agent tool call reaching handler(request) while st.session_state.get('approve', True) is falsy (app.py:100), i.e., a tool invocation executing without the user-approved 'Allow tool calls' permission; in that case the middleware must return ToolMessage('❌ Tool call denied by user') (app.py:101-104) and must not forward the request.
pending_binding_information: The internal dispatch semantics of langchain.agents.middleware.wrap_tool_call and create_agent middleware ordering are framework-supplied and not visible in this source; confirm that human_approval always executes before the tool handler and that the denial ToolMessage fully short-circuits handler(request) for every tool call.

Whether handler(request) can commit effects beyond the two tool bodies' HTTP calls (e.g., if the tool list changes) is not determinable from the supplied source, since the middleware is generic over tool names.

Whether the 'approve' session flag reflects an explicit, deliberate human decision at call time in the deployed environment (vs. the default-allow state) depends on Streamlit session-state isolation and deployment configuration not supplied.
contracts.protected_operation: Agent tool invocation of the get_weather tool (external HTTP request via requests.get to api.openweathermap.org, app.py:30-34) or the get_news tool (external search via tavily_client.search, app.py:56-61), dispatched through the agent's tool-call path.
contracts.protected_resource: External HTTP APIs reached through the agent's tools: the OpenWeather current-weather endpoint URL constructed at app.py:30 and fetched at app.py:33, and the Tavily search API invoked at app.py:57-61, together with the agent tool-dispatch path that gates them.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every agent tool invocation on the create_agent agent (the get_weather and get_news tools, which issue external HTTP calls to the OpenWeather current-weather API and the Tavily search API) must pass through the human_approval @wrap_tool_call middleware before execution; if the user's 'approve' session flag is false, the middleware must return a denial ToolMessage instead of forwarding the call, with the commit point at handler(request) (app.py:106). The two reviewer opinions describe this same guard and are merged into a single obligation.
scope_limits: The guard is fail-open by default: st.session_state.get('approve', True) (app.py:100) and the UI checkbox value=True (app.py:131) both default to allowed, so tool calls execute unless the user explicitly unchecks the flag; the obligation is a denial-when-disabled gate, not an opt-in approval requirement.

The gate reads a static per-session flag, not a live per-call human prompt; approval is not bound to individual tool calls or arguments, and the middleware performs no validation of tool inputs (e.g., the city string is interpolated directly into the URL at app.py:30 and the Tavily query at app.py:58).

Coverage extends only to tool calls on the agent's two registered tools (app.py:114); the LLM invocation itself (agent.invoke at app.py:158-160) and chat-history session-state mutations (app.py:150, app.py:166-169) are not gated by this middleware.

The denial branch returns a ToolMessage to the agent conversation (app.py:101-104); the supplied source does not show any additional enforcement (e.g., rate limiting, auditing) beyond this short-circuit.

Agent mediation is established only for the two tools registered in create_agent (app.py:112-117); the middleware is written generically over request.tool_call and would gate any future tool registered on this agent.
